args.rationale: 69-year-old man with advanced lung adenocarcinoma, deep jaundice, melena, lethargy and lightheadedness. Hemoglobin fell from 123 to 45 g/L. He needs ongoing transfusion, hemodynamic monitoring and urgent endoscopy. The CT showed no hemorrhage or collection. The bleeding source and the cause of the jaundice (immune-mediated hemolysis, GI bleed with cholestasis, or biliary obstruction) are not yet confirmed. Coagulation studies, liver panel and platelets were not available.
args.followup_or_handoff: Continue crossmatched PRBC transfusion and IV pantoprazole. Recheck hemoglobin and hemodynamics after each unit. Obtain INR, platelets, liver panel with fractionated bilirubin, hemolysis workup (LDH, haptoglobin, reticulocytes, DAT, smear) and type and screen as soon as available. Urgent EGD, with duodenoscopy of the ampulla if needed. Clarify the current cancer therapy, especially any immune checkpoint inhibitor, and any anticoagulant, antiplatelet, NSAID or steroid use. Involve oncology, GI/hepatology and hematology. If hemolysis is confirmed, consider steroids in consultation. Hand off that the diagnosis is uncertain.
